description:
FILED s454ad (Opus round 12, agent AD), found by a #755 probe; PRE-EXISTING
(identical on the 154f4a9 base worktree).

    mkdir "/tmp/d"; chdir "/tmp/d";
    my @names = ("plain_a", "plain_b");
    for my $n (@names) { open my $f, ">", $n or die; close $f }
    open my $f, ">", "plain_c" or die; close $f;
    my $cnt = unlink @names, "plain_c";
    print "count=$cnt\n";
        perl: count=3
        PCL:  count=1        (only plain_c is deleted; the files in @names stay)

CAUSE (emission, not runtime): the funcall lowers to (p-unlink @n "c") -- the
pl-array VECTOR is passed as ONE &rest argument, never flattened, and
p-unlink's (to-string (unbox f)) on a vector is not a filename.  The whole
family emits the same shape (probed):

    unlink(@n, "c")   -> (p-unlink @n "c")
    chmod 0644, @n    -> (p-chmod #o644 @n)
    utime 1, 2, @n    -> (p-utime 1 2 @n)
    kill 9, @n        -> (p-kill 9 @n)

(chown presumably too -- same &rest runtime shape.)  Other list builtins get
p-flatten-args; these do not.  FIX SHAPE (not designed): decide the seam --
either these calls' emission flattens like the other list builtins, or the
&rest runtime family maps p-flatten-args over its arguments itself (ONE
helper, rule 11).  Runtime-side flattening also fixes the shape reached
through indirect calls.

BAR: the probe above vs perl for unlink, chmod (mode preserved), utime,
kill (count + delivery), chown; a hash in the list (perl flattens
keys+values); an empty array contributes nothing.
subject: unlink/chmod/utime/kill @array: the array reaches the runtime UNFLATTENED -- one vector argument instead of its elements (perl counts 3, PCL counts 1)
